banner: Pre-release template: placeholder figures, not PolicyEngine estimates

basis.cost: Static, cash, fiscal year, UK unless a measure says otherwise, £ million; positive is a cost to the Exchequer
basis.distribution: Average change in household net income by equivalised household income decile, UK
basis.age_band: Average change in household net income of people in each age band, by their own age
basis.behaviour: No behavioural response: no change in hours, hiring, education or claims

measures.name: Lower youth standard allowance (illustrative)
measures.description: Illustrative age-only stand-in for a separate youth route: the UC standard allowance for single claimants under 25 at 90% of the 2027-28 rate (£317.85 a month).
measures.recommendation: A separate route for young people who have never worked, with less cash and more support
measures.route_reason: The cash part for everyone under 25 is a parameter change. The never-worked test and the support offer are not modelled.

measures.name: Youth route for those who have never worked
measures.description: Young people under 25 who have never worked move to a separate benefit route with a participation offer.
measures.recommendation: A separate route for young people who have never worked, with less cash and more support
measures.route_reason: The data hold no work history. The closest proxy, no earnings in the survey year, includes people who have worked before.

measures.name: No UC health element for new claimants under 22
measures.description: New claimants under 22 get no UC health element and are offered support instead. Shown as a range: from the claimants the model treats as new, up to every claimant under 22.
measures.recommendation: Health element for young people replaced by a support offer
measures.route_reason: An age test applied to the health element before the model sets each claimant's rate. The support offer is not modelled.

measures.name: No UC health element for new claimants under 25
measures.description: As above, for new claimants under 25.
measures.recommendation: Health element for young people replaced by a support offer
measures.route_reason: An age test applied to the health element before the model sets each claimant's rate. The support offer is not modelled.

measures.name: Payment for limited capability for work
measures.description: A smaller payment for young claimants with limited capability for work, in place of the all-or-nothing health element.
measures.recommendation: Graded health support instead of a single health element
measures.route_reason: The model has a limited capability for work flag but no element amount for it; needs a new variable.

measures.name: Higher work allowances (illustrative)
measures.description: Illustrative: UC work allowances 20% higher (£530.33 and £881.82 a month) for all ages, as a stand-in for a youth work allowance.
measures.recommendation: Make it pay for young people to try work
measures.route_reason: The all-ages version is a parameter change. A youth-only work allowance or taper needs an age dimension upstream.

measures.name: Guarantee of work, training or an apprenticeship
measures.description: A job, training place or apprenticeship for every young person who engages, with support and a duty to take up the offer.
measures.recommendation: A guarantee for every young person aged 16 to 24
measures.route_reason: A spending programme. Recorded as a spending line from official figures or a unit cost; a subsidised job's pay can be shown in household examples.

measures.name: Local participation system
measures.description: Upfront funding for combined and local authorities in England to run support for young people.
measures.route_reason: A grant to local government; recorded as a spending line.

measures.name: Employer NICs zero rate to age 25
measures.description: Extend the employer National Insurance zero rate from employees under 21 to employees under 25, up to the upper secondary threshold.
measures.recommendation: Lower the cost of hiring young people
measures.route_reason: The pinned model version does not include the employer zero rate for young employees, so the extension cannot be costed until the model is updated.

measures.name: 18-20 minimum wage at the National Living Wage (illustrative)
measures.description: Illustrative: the 18-20 rate raised to the rate for 21 and over.
measures.recommendation: Minimum wage rates for young workers
measures.route_reason: Earnings are survey inputs, so a wage rate change does not reach pay; only the UC minimum income floor and similar tests read the rate. Employment effects are not modelled.

measures.name: Apprenticeship incentives for employers
measures.description: Larger payments to employers who take on apprentices aged 16 to 24.
measures.route_reason: A payment to employers per apprentice; recorded as a spending line. The pinned data have no apprentice flag.

measures.name: Family support for young people in training to 21 (illustrative)
measures.description: Illustrative: the UC child element and Child Benefit continue for young people in approved education or training until 21 rather than 20.
measures.recommendation: Keep family support while a young person trains
measures.route_reason: The qualifying young person age limits are parameters. A new learning allowance would need a new variable.

measures.name: Learning allowance for young people in training
measures.description: A weekly allowance for young people aged 16 to 24 in approved training, tested on household income.
measures.recommendation: Financial support to stay in learning
measures.route_reason: No such allowance in the model; needs a new variable reading approved training and household income.

measures.name: PIP for young people aged 16 to 24
measures.description: Changes to PIP for young people, such as a participation plan alongside or in place of a daily living award.
measures.recommendation: Health and disability support for young people
measures.route_reason: PIP rates are parameters but have no age dimension; any age rule needs a new formula. PIP applies in England and Wales.

measures.name: Mental health support for young people
measures.description: Faster access to mental health support for under-25s.
measures.route_reason: A health service measure; recorded as a spending line.

measures.name: Track every young person; raise the participation age
measures.description: A duty to track young people to 24 and a higher participation age in England.
measures.recommendation: Know where every young person is
measures.route_reason: An administrative duty; recorded as a spending line if costed.

measures.name: Shared accommodation rate to age 25 (illustrative)
measures.description: Illustrative: single renters aged 25 to 34 move from the shared accommodation rate to the one-bedroom rate.
measures.route_reason: The age threshold is a parameter; modelled directly.

measures.name: Shared accommodation rate exemptions for care leavers
measures.description: Wider exemptions from the shared accommodation rate for care leavers and other young people at risk.
measures.route_reason: The data have no care-leaver flag, and the model does not observe the existing care-leaver and hostel exceptions.

data_limits.reason: Earnings are survey inputs. A change to a minimum wage rate does not change anyone's pay; only the UC minimum income floor, the benefit cap exception and similar tests read the rate. Hiring and hours effects are not modelled.
The data hold the PIP award level, not the assessment points behind it, so a change to the points needed for an award cannot be costed. Changes to the weekly rates can.
No work history. The closest proxy, no earnings in the survey year, includes young people who have worked before.
No flag for being out of education, employment or training, or for how long. A proxy is built from employment status, education and approved training, and is not calibrated to the ONS count.
No Work Capability Assessment outcome. The health element group is inferred from disability-benefit receipt.

The survey does not record who has left care, so the data have no care-leaver flag and the shared accommodation rate exceptions for care leavers are not observed. Care leavers could be shown only as example households.

No apprentice flag in the pinned national build. Later builds impute apprentices among employees aged 21 to 24 to size the employer National Insurance relief, from a small number of survey records, so effects on apprentices alone could be shown only as example households, not as national totals.
Employees under 21 are not a separate calibration target. The employer National Insurance relief for them is checked against HMRC's estimate on the data used for publication.
Few survey records cover 16- and 17-year-olds on Universal Credit, so figures for them are national only and are not split by region.
No employer records, hiring or job-to-job flows, so employment effects of wages and incentives are not modelled.

model_limits.reason: The pinned model version does not include the employer National Insurance zero rate for employees under 21 or apprentices under 25, so a change to it cannot be costed until the model is updated. Later model versions (from policyengine-uk 2.165.1) include it.

The pinned model version holds the April 2027 minimum wage rates at £12.71, £10.85 and £8.00 an hour, against the published £13.21, £11.27 and £8.31. Later model versions (from policyengine-uk 2.168.0) carry the published rates.

From 2026-27 the model sets each claimant's UC health element directly, at the protected rate for claims made before April 2026 and the lower rate for later claims. A change to the element's own amount therefore has no effect; changes are written against the two rates, or as an age test applied before that step.

Which claimants get the lower health element rate for claims made from April 2026 is assigned at random, at the same share for every age (13% in 2027-28). Young claimants are more likely to be recent claimants, so a measure for new young claimants is shown as a range: from that share up to every young claimant.

Under the Universal Credit Act 2025 the protected health element rate is set so that, with each standard allowance, it keeps its value. Lowering the under-25 standard allowance would therefore raise the protected rate for claimants of every age. The measures here hold the protected rate at its current-law path, so the change reaches only the standard allowance.

Whether a claimant has limited capability for work-related activity follows receipt of disability benefits in the data, not an assessment outcome. The total for 16-24-year-olds is close to the official count, but who is in the group may differ; this is checked against the official figures on the day.
UC work allowances and the taper do not vary by age in the model, so an all-ages change stands in for a change for young people only and reaches claimants of every age.
The under-25 standard allowance for single claimants does not cover couples where both partners are under 25, who have their own rate.
PIP has no country test in the model, and Scotland's Adult Disability Payment is recorded as PIP in the data. PIP measures are shown for England and Wales only.
